text.p: AirWays Corp and ValuJet Inc said Thursday they have signed an agreement to merge to form a new airline holding company called AirTran Holdings Inc.

The deal calls for ValuJet to acquire AirWays in a one-for-one stock swap, they said. ValuJet also would issue about 9.07 million shares of stock valued at about $61.8 million, based on ValuJet's closing share price of $6.81 on July 9.
The merger is subject to shareholder, bondholder, regulatory and certain other approvals, they said. The final merger and closing date are anticipated to occur within three to four months.
The combination has been structured as a tax-free merger, they said. The carriers -- AirTran Airways and ValuJet Airlines -- will continue to function under their respective operating certificates.
The location of the holding company's headquarters is under review, with Orlando, Fla., currently the lead candidate, they said.
ValuJet will nominate four members to the board of directors of the combined entity, while AirWays will nominate three, they said.

D. Joseph Corr, who joined ValuJet in November 1996 as president and chief executive officer, will serve in the same capacities of the combined company, they said. Corr previously served as chairman, president and CEO of Continental Airlines Inc and as president of Trans World Airlines Inc.
Robert Swenson, chairman, president and chief executive officer of AirWays will serve as a non-executive chairman of the combined company.
The combined company would have 2,742 employees and would serve 46 cities with 238 peak daily departures and a fleet of 40 aircraft, they said.

"This agreement provides an excellent opportunity to combine two complementary business plans and provide access to reliable service and affordable fares to large markets currently served by ValuJet and mid-sized cities with AirTran service," Corr said in a written statement.

"The merged company will benefit from access to AirWays' maintenance facility in Orlando and the ValuJet launch order for 50 firm and 50 option McDonnell Douglas MD-95s with delivery scheduled to begin in June 1999," he said.

"The companies have many synergies including affordable fares, a focus on the leisure traveler and some of the industry's most dedicated and experienced employees," Swenson said. "This merger should significantly enhance AirTran's growth prospects with the strong cash position of the merged companies and our combined operating fleet total of more than 40 aircraft."
AirTran Airways provides service between Orlando and 23 cities with a fleet of Boeing 737 aircraft, it said. The carrier is expecting delivery of its 11th Boeing 737 aircraft by the end of July.
Atlanta-based ValuJet Airlines currently operates 200 system-wide peak daily departures to 24 cities with a fleet of 30 aircraft.
